name: Toast, Inc.
thesis: Toast is the leading cloud operating system for restaurants, integrating point-of-sale hardware, kitchen display systems, payment processing, online ordering, and workforce management across >100k restaurant locations. The thesis seeds focus on Toast's agentic AI rollout—specifically Toast IQ Grow reaching $10M ARR at record velocity by automating guest marketing campaigns and cutting restaurant agency spend by 70%, with a roadmap to automate bookkeeping and tax. However, an independent thesis requires scrutinizing the business model realities: Toast is predominantly a payments processor with ~27% consolidated gross margin, making revenue and take-rates sensitive to dining macro cycles and restaurant closure rates (SMB churn). Additionally, small restaurant owners are highly price-conscious, creating uncertainty around long-term pricing power for AI agent add-ons. TOST is placed on the evaluation list to track Toast IQ ARR traction, SaaS gross profit expansion, and FCF compounding ($608M in FY25 with declining SBC) against restaurant sector discretionary trends.
key_driver: Toast IQ agentic SaaS monetization + location density vs SMB restaurant churn and fintech take-rate compression

thesis_breakers_qualitative: SMB restaurant closure rates spike, driving net location additions negative and creating bad-debt/processing chargebacks
Square or Clover initiates aggressive hardware/software fee discounting that erodes Toast take-rates and subscription pricing
Toast IQ agentic tools fail to demonstrate measurable ROI or customer conversion for restaurant operators, resulting in high churn
Payment processing regulatory interventions or interchange fee caps severely compress net fintech gross profit
Free cash flow conversion stalls due to rising customer acquisition costs or heightened hardware subsidies

break_rules.narrative: Revenue growth below 12% signals market saturation or severe restaurant sector macro contraction.
Gross margin falling below 22% indicates severe payment processing margin erosion or excessive hardware discounting.
